Identity.History: The Temple of Athena Nike, built on the southwest bastion of the Athenian Acropolis around 427–424 BC, was a small but elegant Ionic temple dedicated to Athena in her aspect as bringer of victory. Designed by Kallikrates, it housed a cult image of the goddess and overlooked the approach to the Acropolis, making its military symbolism especially prominent. Its surrounding parapet was decorated with graceful reliefs of Nike figures, including the famous image of Nike adjusting her sandal.
